title: Medical and sales representatives
author: Editorial Desk
summary: An often overlooked white-collar workforce with a BMS federation.
body:
The **Bharatiya Medical & Sales Representatives' Mahasangh** represents people who work as medical representatives and sales promotion staff, mainly in pharmaceutical and consumer goods companies.

## A special law

The **Sales Promotion Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1976** gives such employees some of the protections of workmen, including leave, hours and wages. It now forms part of the labour codes.

## Issues

- **Targets and incentives** that put pressure on staff.
- **Termination** and retrenchment during mergers.
- **Digital detailing** and the effect of technology on field jobs.
- Access to **social security** for employees on contracts through third parties.

## Why the sector matters

Medical representatives link doctors with products. Fair and ethical practice in this link matters to patients as well. BMS has supported guidelines against inducements and in favour of ethical marketing.

## The lesson

White-collar workers also need unions. In the age of targets and dashboards, stress is a safety issue.
